Intermediate: A booking list includes appointment 71 with no assigned room. Which join shows this appointment and what appears in room-name columns?
A left join from appointments retains 71 and supplies NULL for the missing room name.
A directory needs only employees with a matching department row. Which join and matching fields fit?
Use an inner join matching the employee department ID to the department's ID.
A member has two loans and appears twice after joining members to loans. Why are both rows valid for a loan-level report?
The member matches two loan records, and each output row represents one matched loan.
Two branches share a name but have different IDs. Which column should join parcels to branches and why?
Join on the branch ID because a name can match multiple branches.
A ticket has separate origin and destination station IDs pointing to the same station table. How can one query retrieve both station names?
Join the station table twice using different aliases, once for each station role.
Advanced: A customer report uses LEFT JOIN orders and WHERE orders.status = 'open', then loses customers with no orders. How can it keep them while counting only open orders?
Move the open-status restriction into the join condition and count matching order IDs.
join condition/on clause
count/order ids
A report joins one ₹60 invoice with three lines and two payments and gets six combinations. How can the original fact totals be preserved?
Aggregate the lines and payments separately to one row per invoice before joining the summaries.
separately/aggregate
one row/invoice
Two tables have 5 and 8 records. A join accidentally returns 40 rows. What missing condition should be investigated?
Inspect the join predicate because an unconstrained Cartesian product pairs every left row with every right row.
predicate/condition
cartesian/every
Attendance rows reference room IDs that no longer exist. Why does a normal inner join hide the issue and what audit would expose it?
An inner join discards unmatched rows. Use a left join or anti-join to list missing room matches.
unmatched/discard
left/anti-join
A vendor ID is only unique within its city. A join matches on vendor ID alone. Which key and test reveal and repair the error?
Match city and vendor ID together and test two cities containing the same vendor ID.
city
same vendor/composite/together

Intermediate: Delivery times are 5, 10 and 15 minutes. How does a nested average identify trips slower than their group?
The inner average returns 10, and the outer greater-than filter retains 15.
A shop wants customers who placed at least one order. Which subquery test asks only whether a matching row exists?
Use EXISTS with a match on the outer customer's ID.
A teacher compares every pupil's mark with the average for that pupil's own class. Which value from the outer row belongs in the inner query?
Correlate the inner rows by the outer pupil's class ID before averaging.
A supervisor compares a fee with a nested query returning one regional fee. What must be true of its number of results?
It must supply one meaningful scalar value for that comparison; multiple regional rows need disambiguation.
A clerk needs products in the set of categories requested by a buyer. Which operator compares a category with a list returned by a subquery?
Use IN to test category membership in the returned category values.
Advanced: A list of returned-book IDs includes NULL. Why might NOT IN fail to find a valid unreturned book and which expression is safer?
The missing value can make the comparison unknown. Use NOT EXISTS correlated on book ID.
unknown/null
not exists
A scalar fee query returned several fee rows after the firm added another branch. Why is LIMIT 1 without a rule a fragile repair?
It selects an arbitrary reference fee. Match the intended branch or define a business rule selecting one applicable row.
arbitrary/undefined
branch/business rule
A correlated price query is slow for a large orders table. What alternative and correctness check would you try?
Precompute grouped reference prices and join them by group ID; compare results on empty or missing groups too.
grouped/precompute
compare/missing/empty
A branch-average benchmark uses future deliveries to judge yesterday's courier. Which two scopes should restrict the inner query?
Restrict the reference data to the relevant branch and the time window available at the assessment date.
branch
time/date
A team replaces EXISTS with a join and customer counts rise despite matching eligibility rules. Where did the extra rows come from?
Several matching orders can duplicate one customer in a join. EXISTS returns one yes/no decision per outer customer.
duplicate/several/multiple
yes/no decision/one decision/outer customer

Intermediate: Two sales of 20 and 30 belong to East and one sale of 8 belongs to West. What are the East count and total?
The East group contains two sales totaling 50.
A clinic has six appointments but only four supplied phone numbers. Which two counts produce 6 and 4?
COUNT(*) counts all six rows and COUNT(phone) counts the four non-NULL phone entries.
A shop wants only stalls earning more than 100 across the day. Which clause tests each stall's finished total?
Group by stall and use HAVING on its sum.
A manufacturer wants daily production totals for one specific factory. Which filter runs before the grouping?
Select that factory's rows with WHERE and group the remaining rows by production day.
A supplier's rows include 10 units, 0 units and a missing amount. Which known quantities contribute to AVG(amount)?
AVG includes 10 and zero and skips the NULL, giving an average of 5.
Advanced: One till averages 10 minutes over one visit and another averages 20 over nine. Why is the combined customer average 19?
Weight each mean by its visit count: the total is 190 minutes for 10 visits.
weight/visit count
190/10 visits
A team groups sales by product name. Two separate products share the name Classic. What should the grouping key represent?
Group by a stable product ID, then attach the label for display so distinct products remain separate.
product id/stable
label/display
A tracker averages delivery time only for completed deliveries. Why can it look faster while a growing queue waits?
Pending deliveries are excluded from the completed sample. Report backlog size or waiting age alongside that mean.
pending/excluded
backlog/waiting
A revenue report gains extra money after joining sales to tags. Why can't SUM(DISTINCT amount) reliably repair the total?
Different sales may share amounts. Preserve one row per sale ID before summing, irrespective of tag count.
share amounts/same amount/equal
sale id/one row
A report groups timestamps by UTC date, but a shop closes its day at local midnight. How should the grouping definition change?
Convert each event into the shop's local time zone before deriving the business date for grouping.
local/time zone
date/day

Intermediate: A catalog frequently retrieves one product by barcode. Which candidate index matches this pattern and what plan evidence is relevant?
Index the barcode and check whether the query plan uses a selective index lookup.
A shop adds an index on stock quantity. What extra work happens when a quantity changes?
The engine updates the table row and maintains the corresponding index entry.
A query returns almost every row in a small table. Why might a full scan be a reasonable plan?
Low selectivity means most rows are needed and scanning can avoid extra index traversal.
A service commonly filters by branch ID and sorts by time within a branch. Which index column order might support both operations?
Consider a composite index on branch ID followed by time.
A bookstore wants to compare lookups before and after an index. What should stay the same besides the database engine?
Use the same data and query workload, and verify identical result rows.
Advanced: A composite index begins with region and then account ID. Why might searching only account ID get little benefit?
Entries are ordered primarily by region, so an account-only search may lack a useful leading-key restriction.
region/leading
account/restriction
A query uses lower(email) but the index is on raw email. What alternatives would you test before promising an improvement?
Inspect the plan and consider an expression index or normalized stored key matching the actual comparison.
plan
expression index/normalized
A table is write-heavy and has five rarely used indexes. What measurements justify removing one?
Measure query use and latency dependent on that index, then compare write throughput and storage with it removed.
query/latency
write/storage
A plan switches from an index to a table scan after a filter changes from one user to an entire city. Why might this be expected?
The city filter matches a larger fraction of rows. A scan may be cheaper than many index-driven table reads.
fraction/selectivity
scan/cheaper
A student treats seeing an index name in EXPLAIN as proof a query is fast. What evidence still matters for the decision?
Measure actual latency on representative data and account for rows visited, maintenance cost and workload.
latency/measure
representative/workload

Intermediate: A wallet transfer moves 3 credits from 8 to an account holding 2. What two balances should appear after a successful atomic transfer?
The source becomes 5 and the destination becomes 5, keeping the total at 10.
A checkout reserved a seat, then failed before recording the booking in the same transaction. What database action restores the earlier state?
Roll back the transaction so its uncommitted reservation is discarded.
When should a cashier announce that a multi-row purchase has been saved?
Confirm after all required changes succeed and the transaction commits.
A user changes two contact fields together but chooses Cancel before confirming. What operation should discard those unsaved database edits?
Use rollback on the active transaction before commit.
A bank transfer must reject a nonexistent destination. Which checks belong before reporting success?
Verify both account matches and commit the debit and credit together only when both succeed.
Advanced: Two ticket desks each read one remaining seat and both promise it to customers. Why is checking before a separate update unsafe?
The earlier read can become stale. Use an atomic conditional update or equivalent lock and verify one successful reservation.
stale/concurrent
atomic/lock
A transfer commits just before its reply is lost. How can a retry avoid transferring funds twice?
Send a stable idempotency key and atomically record or reuse the result for that key.
idempotency/request id
atomic/reuse
A checkout transaction also emits an external email, then rolls back locally. Why can't the database undo the email?
Email is an external side effect outside the transaction. Queue a committed outbox record and dispatch it with duplicate handling.
external/outside
outbox/dispatch
Two workers transfer stock between the same warehouses in opposite directions and each waits for the other. What strategy reduces deadlocks?
Acquire locks in a consistent warehouse order and retry a transaction abandoned by deadlock detection.
consistent/order
retry/deadlock detection
A report reads total credits and then individual balances while other transfers occur. What guarantee helps those reads describe the same moment?
Use a consistent transaction snapshot or isolation level that preserves one view across the reads.
snapshot/isolation
one view/same moment/across

Intermediate: A shop stores the supplier's current phone number separately on every product. Which relationship removes repeated updates?
Keep one supplier record and let products reference its supplier ID.
A pupil enrolls in two courses and each course admits many pupils. What should one enrollment row contain?
Store the pupil ID and course ID as one link, with a uniqueness rule if duplicate enrollment is forbidden.
A company wants past invoices to show the delivery address used at purchase. Should they look up only the customer's current address?
Store an invoice address snapshot because the current address can change after delivery.
A bookstore lets several copies share a title and author. Where should a single copy's damage note be saved?
Put the note on the identified copy, while the title record stores information shared by copies.
A table links each order to one known customer. What rule should prevent an order referencing customer 999 when no such customer exists?
Enforce a foreign key from the order's customer ID to the customer table's key.
Advanced: A team proposes storing comma-separated allergy labels in one pupil field, then searching labels using substrings. What can go wrong and what design improves the query?
Substrings can match unintended labels. Use a linked pupil-allergy table with one relationship per row.
substring/unintended
link/relationship
A store denormalizes product names into a search table for speed. What source of truth and maintenance obligation should be explicit?
Keep the product record authoritative and define how derived search entries refresh after a name change.
authoritative/source of truth
refresh/derived
A customer has several valid addresses and changes a default. Why might putting only an address string on each order be insufficient for address management?
Separate customer address records support multiple choices and defaults, while each order keeps its own historical delivery snapshot.
multiple/default
snapshot/historical
A team makes email the only account key, then allows customers to change or share an email. Which assumption failed and what safer identity follows?
Email lacks stable uniqueness under that policy. Use an independent account ID and model email as changeable contact data.
stable/unique
account id/independent
A survey stores a blank answer, an unanswered question and an inapplicable question all as empty text. What reporting error and design correction follow?
Completion counts can mix different states. Represent response status explicitly and store the answer separately when supplied.
count/completion
status/separately

Intermediate: A library register has one line per member and one column for membership expiry. What does one row describe and where is the expiry found?
A row describes one member; expiry is read from that member's expiry column.
A clinic has two patients named Arun. What should reception use to select one record for an address update?
Use a unique patient ID to identify a single row before changing the address.
An app should list students after a power cycle. Which step makes a newly entered student persist?
Save and commit the record to persistent storage before confirming registration.
A volunteer has no recorded phone number but has a valid card number. What can the database record without inventing contact data?
Store the known card identity and mark the phone value as missing or NULL.
A manager asks how many members have expired cards, rather than requesting their complete contact records. What should the query return?
Filter rows by the expiry condition and return a count of matching members.
Advanced: A person can hold multiple library loans. Why would one row per person with a single book-title field lose information?
A new loan would replace the previous loan value. Store loans as separate rows linked to the member.
replace/overwrite
separate/link
A warehouse operator edits a product name while another user records a delivery against that product. Why should the delivery refer to a stable ID?
A name can change or repeat, while the ID preserves the identity of the linked product.
change/repeat
identity/link/id
A team believes a backup is usable because the backup file exists. What test would demonstrate recovery of the member register?
Restore into a separate database and verify known members, counts and related records there.
restore
verify/count/known
A deletion request for a member leaves loans pointing to a missing account. What relationship policy should have been defined?
Define referential integrity for loans and choose whether deletion is restricted, cascaded or replaced by retaining a historical member record.
referential/foreign key
restrict/cascade/historical
A manager counts members by counting registration events. Returning members register again every term. What quantity should be counted instead?
Count distinct stable member IDs over the desired group, and keep event count as a separate measure.
distinct/unique
member id/identit

Intermediate: A courier wants ready parcels weighing at most 3 kg. Which two conditions must be combined and how?
Combine ready status and weight <= 3 with AND so both apply to every selected parcel.
A teacher wants only the name and mark in a result, although the table has many columns. Which clause supplies the fields to display?
SELECT names the two required columns, while FROM identifies the marks table.
A desk wants the three newest orders. What operation should precede LIMIT 3?
Order by creation time descending and use an ID tie-breaker when times match.
A register uses NULL for unknown phone numbers. Which predicate finds those rows and why is ordinary equality unsuitable?
Use IS NULL; equality with NULL yields unknown rather than a true match.
A club requires membership or a guest voucher, plus age at least 18 for everyone. How should the two parts be grouped?
Group membership OR voucher together, then AND the age requirement with that result.
Advanced: A sorted report changes page membership between calls because many orders have the same date. Which additional rule makes the ordering deterministic?
Add a unique tie-breaker such as order ID to the date ordering so equal-date rows have a defined sequence.
unique/tie-breaker
sequence/order
A search for names starting with A includes user-supplied search text. Which two concerns arise if the input contains a quote or a percent sign?
Bind the value as a parameter for SQL safety and escape wildcard characters when literal matching is intended.
parameter/bind
wildcard/percent/escape
A bike dispatcher queries weight <= 3 and assumes the remaining parcels all exceed 3 kg. Which records disprove that claim and how should they be reported?
Unknown weights produce an unknown predicate and are excluded as well. Report missing weights separately.
unknown/null
separately/missing
A store wants orders from a single calendar day, but its timestamps include times. What filter avoids losing orders near the end of the day?
Use a half-open range from the day's start inclusive to the next day's start exclusive in the intended time zone.
inclusive/start
exclusive/next day
A report filters for names and another process changes rows while results are read in pages. Why might deterministic ordering alone fail to reproduce the original result?
The underlying rows can change between pages. Use a consistent snapshot or defined cursor strategy for the required semantics.
change/insert/delete
snapshot/cursor

Intermediate: A guide must search saved routes on one tablet with no network. Why might local SQLite fit the lookup?
The engine can query a local file without a connection to a remote service.
Five branches need one current stock figure and can connect reliably. Which storage arrangement gives them an authoritative shared value?
Send updates to a common database service and coordinate changes there using transactions.
A developer moves an application from SQLite to PostgreSQL. Which query properties should a small compatibility fixture check?
Verify returned values and ordering under the target engine, and verify expected invalid inputs are rejected.
A shop laptop loses internet access during lunch. What part of a local-first billing design lets it continue selling, and what later task remains?
Save sales locally while disconnected, then synchronize accepted sales with the central store later.
A student asks why both engines can answer SELECT name FROM employees even though they are deployed differently. What is shared and what differs?
Both implement common SQL operations, but one can run embedded while the other commonly serves networked clients.
Advanced: A company synchronizes writable copies of a SQLite file across branches using a file-sharing service. Why is that unsafe for concurrent sales?
File syncing does not coordinate database transactions across copies. Use a shared writer service or application-level synchronization of changes.
transaction/concurrent
shared writer/synchronization of changes
A team chooses PostgreSQL for a lone offline kiosk because a larger engine sounds faster. What workload and operating costs should be compared first?
Measure the actual local lookup and write workload and compare service setup, connectivity and maintenance costs.
workload/measure
maintenance/connectivity/setup
A uniqueness test passes on one database and fails on another with mixed-case email addresses. Which semantic detail should migration tests cover?
Check the collation or normalized comparison policy and verify that uniqueness uses the intended case handling.
collation/normaliz
unique/case
A central inventory service is unreachable and two branches sell the last item offline. What policy is needed before eventual sync can promise correct stock?
Define reservation or branch allocation limits while offline and a conflict resolution process when sales synchronize.
reservation/allocation
conflict/reconcile
A team copies a production database file during active writes and calls it a verified backup. How can recovery risk be reduced?
Use the engine's supported consistent backup mechanism and regularly test restoring it into a separate environment.
consistent/backup mechanism
restore/restoring

Intermediate: A membership number '0004' must print with four digits and never be added to another member number. What column type suits it?
Use text so the leading zeroes survive storage and retrieval.
A workshop has a required seat count that must exceed zero. Which two constraints express presence and range?
Require NOT NULL and add a check that the count is greater than zero.
A shop records ₹12.50 using integer paise. What value is stored and which unit should the column name communicate?
Store 1250 and name or document the column as paise.
A contact list allows unknown emails but prohibits two members from sharing a card number. Which property should the card column have?
Enforce uniqueness and require a nonmissing card number for each member.
A school needs one row for each pupil. What should one identifier do when two pupils have the same full name?
A primary key must distinguish the two rows even though their names match.
Advanced: A developer adds CHECK (amount > 0) but some missing amounts still pass. What independent rule is required if a value is compulsory?
Add NOT NULL because a check involving NULL may evaluate to unknown without rejecting the row.
not null
unknown/null
A new table constraint rejects negative legacy balances. How should a team introduce the constraint without silently altering account meaning?
Audit the existing negative records, resolve them under a documented policy, then enforce the constraint.
audit/existing
policy/enforce
A store wants case-insensitively unique coupon codes. Why can a plain uniqueness rule on raw text be insufficient?
Its comparisons may distinguish case. Enforce uniqueness on a normalized code or suitable collation matching the policy.
case
normalized/collation
A timestamp column formerly meant local clock time but clients now span several regions. What must migration specify to preserve event order?
Establish the original time zone for historical values and convert to an unambiguous instant with documented display rules.
time zone/zone
instant/utc/unambiguous
A schema records all prices in integer minor units. Why is the value 100 alone insufficient for a store handling several currencies?
Store the currency identity and know its minor-unit scale to interpret 100 correctly.
currency
scale/precision

Intermediate: Order 41 currently contains two coffees and the customer adds one. Which operation and filter update only this order?
UPDATE the quantity for the row whose order ID equals 41.
A volunteer needs to see an existing order without changing it. Which operation and identifier should be used?
SELECT the order using its unique order ID.
A team creates a new customer and then needs a reliable reference for her first order. What should the creation step return?
Insert the customer and obtain its assigned primary key for the order link.
A shop attempts to cancel order 500, which is absent. What result should it check before confirming cancellation?
Check the affected row count and report that no matching order was found when it is zero.
A club must keep an order for audits while hiding it from active orders. What alternative to deletion fits?
Update its status to cancelled and filter active-order views using that status.
Advanced: A customer double-clicks Create Order and two identical paid orders appear. How can retries reuse the first creation result?
Store a unique idempotency key with the created order and return the existing result for repeated requests.
idempotency/unique request
existing/repeated
Two dispatchers edit the same order from old screens, and the second overwrites the first. Which conditional update detects the conflict?
Include the previously read version in the update condition and reject a stale change if zero rows match.
version
zero/stale
A bulk cleanup will delete expired reservations. How could you preview its intended effect and keep the final action consistent with that preview?
Inspect the IDs selected by the predicate, then execute a guarded deletion in a transaction under suitable concurrency control.
ids/predicate/preview
transaction/concurrency
An update built from a typed customer name fails for O'Neil and could allow an altered SQL command. What should change at the query boundary?
Use a parameterized statement and bind the name separately as a data value.
parameter/bind
data value/separately
A refund updates both order status and stock, but a crash leaves only the status changed. Which operations belong together and what should happen on failure?
Group the refund status and stock adjustment in one transaction and roll it back on failure.
transaction/together

Intermediate: A cart and a receipt printer both need the same service-charge rule. Where should the common calculation live and how should callers access it?
Put the rule in a shared module and import its calculation from both callers.
A script calls fees.total but Python does not know the name fees. Which step was omitted before the call?
Import the fees module so its name is bound in the caller's namespace.
A team groups receipt, menu and pricing modules beneath cafe. What does a package give these related files?
A package groups related modules and gives them a common import namespace.
Two modules define load. How can one script call each operation without ambiguous bare names?
Import the modules under distinct names and qualify each call with its module.
A tester needs the menu's calculation without starting the till screen. Which code should be kept outside the reusable calculation?
Keep the interactive input and display in the entry point and import the calculation independently.
Advanced: A local numbers.py hides the intended third-party package with the same name. What evidence should you collect before reinstalling packages?
Inspect the imported module's file location and the search path to establish which file Python chose.
location/file
search path/sys.path
Importing checkout opens a payment terminal during documentation generation. Why did an import have this effect and how should startup be arranged?
Top-level statements run during import. Put terminal startup behind an explicit entry point.
top-level/import time
entry point/main
The stock module imports checkout and checkout imports stock; startup sees an unavailable attribute. What design removes the dependency cycle?
Extract their shared rule to a third module and arrange imports in one direction.
shared/third module
one direction/acyclic
A program changes a constant in a module after another module used from fees import rate. Why might the second module still see an old value?
The import bound a local name to the earlier object. Read the current attribute through the module or pass the rate explicitly.
local name/bound/binding
attribute/pass the rate
An application caches today's price list while importing the pricing module. Why can a long-running worker show yesterday's prices?
Import-time data remains in memory. Add explicit refresh or version-aware lookup when freshness matters.
import-time/memory/cache
refresh/version

Intermediate: A school and a newsletter need different versions of the same package. How should installs be divided?
Create one environment per project and install the version each project requires.
A terminal shows the right environment name but the IDE cannot import a dependency. Which setting and evidence should be checked?
Check the IDE interpreter path and inspect installed packages using that interpreter.
A student needs to install a package for the exact interpreter running app.py. Which invocation links the installer to that interpreter?
Invoke that Python executable with -m pip, then verify the package imports in the same interpreter.
A teammate receives just the source code on a fresh PC. Which project file helps recreate the package environment?
Provide a dependency specification with the required versions and install it into a fresh environment.
A student deactivates the project environment. What changes for shell commands and what happens to installed project packages?
Shell command resolution changes back, while the project packages remain installed in the environment.
Advanced: A team chooses a fresh virtual environment for executing unknown uploaded Python. What security property is missing?
Package isolation does not restrict filesystem or network permissions. Use a separate restricted execution sandbox.
permission/filesystem/network
sandbox/restricted
Two developers install the same named dependencies without recording versions, and only one reproduces a bug. What should be captured for diagnosis?
Record resolved dependency versions and the Python interpreter version or platform for each environment.
dependency versions/resolved
interpreter/platform
A copied environment works on one laptop and fails after moving the folder on another. Why should recreation be preferred?
Environment files can contain absolute paths and platform-specific binaries. Rebuild from recorded versions on the target system.
paths/binaries/platform
rebuild/recreate
A package upgrade fixes project A but breaks project B although their environments were believed separate. How do you test separation directly?
Compare the interpreter and package installation paths for both projects, then inspect the actual version imported by each.
paths/interpreter
version/imported
A service must remain available during a risky dependency upgrade. How should testing and rollout use environments?
Build and test a separate new environment first, then switch the service with a known previous environment available for rollback.
separate/test
rollback/previous

Intermediate: A designer changed the menu and a private note. How should she prepare a commit containing only the menu change?
Stage the intended menu file or hunk and inspect the staged difference before committing.
A cook wants to inspect a price before a mistaken edit. Which stored information lets the team recover it?
Look at the earlier commit's snapshot and compare the tracked menu file.
A shop wants to try a seasonal menu without replacing the current menu's development history. What Git feature helps?
Create a branch from the current commit and develop the seasonal changes on that branch.
Two cooks each edit a different line. Which operation combines their histories and what should they inspect afterward?
Merge the changes and review the resulting menu for the intended combined behavior.
A volunteer commits locally but a teammate on another machine cannot see it. Which second step makes the commit available on their shared service?
Push the local commit to the shared remote so the teammate can fetch it.
Advanced: A shared branch has a published mistake. Why might a revert be easier on teammates than rewriting the branch history?
Revert adds a correcting commit while retaining the existing commits that teammates already reference.
correcting/new commit
retaining/existing/history
A password was committed and later deleted. What must happen to the credential itself and why?
Rotate or revoke the credential because the old commit or copies may still contain it.

A conflict in tax rate lines has two apparently valid percentages. How should a reviewer choose the resolution?
Check the applicable business policy and test the final agreed percentage on a representative bill.

A bug appears somewhere among 30 commits whose builds are reproducible. How could a team find the introducing commit efficiently?
Use a repeatable pass/fail check with bisection between known good and bad revisions.
repeatable/test

A developer committed a refactor and a behavior change together. Why is a later rollback risky and what future practice would help?
Reverting the mixed commit can undo unrelated work. Commit logically separate changes independently.
unrelated/mixed
separate/independent

Intermediate: A bakery wants the earliest numbered customer served first. Which structure and operations express that service rule?
Enqueue new customers at the back and dequeue the front of a queue.
A photo editor must undo its most recent crop before restoring an earlier brightness change. Which structure fits?
Use a stack and pop the last action first.
A sports desk needs to look up a registered team name by its unique number repeatedly. Which structure fits and what should be the key?
Use a dictionary mapping the team number to its name.
A student needs the unique topics studied across two notebooks. Which structure and combination operation will remove repeated topics?
Put topics into sets and take their union.
A box contains unnumbered receipts in arrival order. Why can a simple search require reading every receipt?
Without a sorted key or lookup structure, a target may be last or absent.
Advanced: A hospital must sometimes serve an emergency before earlier ordinary arrivals. Why would a plain queue implement the wrong rule and what structure would fit?
FIFO ignores urgency. Use a priority queue with arrival order as a tie-breaker.
urgency/priority
tie/arrival
A document editor supports both Undo and Redo. After undoing two edits the user types a new word. What records should change?
Push the new edit onto undo history and clear the old redo branch because it no longer follows the current document.
undo
clear/redo branch
A device must find a member quickly and also list members in enrollment order. Which facts should its representation preserve?
Preserve stable order for listing and provide a membership index or set for fast lookups.
order
index/set
A path checker tracks counts of opening and closing brackets but accepts ([)]. Why is counting insufficient and what invariant should be checked?
Matching counts ignore nesting order. Use a stack and require every closer to match the latest unmatched opener.
nesting/order
latest/stack
A help desk queue processes new jobs continuously. How can always serving the highest urgency class strand low-priority jobs?
A steady flow of urgent jobs can cause starvation. Introduce an aging or fairness rule and measure waiting times.
starvation/indefinitely
aging/fairness

Intermediate: A clerk checks one parcel after another. How does the missing-parcel case change when the tray doubles from 50 to 100 labels?
It doubles from 50 to 100 checks because every label is examined once.
A sorted directory halves its candidates after each comparison. What happens to the number of checks when a directory roughly doubles in size?
It usually adds about one check because one halving returns to the earlier search size.
A shop saves every visitor ID to detect repeats. What storage grows as new people arrive?
The seen set grows with the number of distinct visitor IDs.
A till keeps only a running total while reading a million sale amounts one by one. What additional working storage is required by the summing procedure?
A fixed number of running values suffices apart from representation size, so it avoids storing every sale.
A class compares all pairs of 4 runners once. Why is the work more than simply visiting each runner?
Each runner is paired with several others, giving six distinct pairs for four runners.
Advanced: A programmer promises binary search will speed up one lookup in an unsorted receipt file. Which cost does that promise omit?
It omits sorting the file first. Compare total setup plus lookup cost against a single linear scan.
sorting/setup
single linear scan/total
A dashboard shows average lookup time on tiny inputs and labels an algorithm O(1). What evidence is missing?
Measure a range of growing input sizes and examine how work scales under representative and worst-case inputs.
